1→---
title: dora harness
description: Grill a routine, freeze a Fixed step, then boot it. Dora prints Runtime watch.
sidebar:
  label: Harness
  order: 2
---

`dora harness` is the front desk for an internal teammate. The Runtime ticks the Loop. Today that Runtime is Hermes. A **routine** is the saved folder at `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`. Dora does not install Hermes and does not run the MCP login.
10→
## Before you start

Install [Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/). Reload the shell so `hermes` is on `PATH`. Bring your own LLM credits. Paste a Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP URL when the grill asks.

Missing Hermes prints official install steps and stops. Dora does not fake a test run.

## Create a routine

Type this in the agent:
20→
```text
/ask-dora turn this loop-able check into a routine
```

The same door from the CLI is `dora harness new`. Bare `new` starts `ask-dora`, which loads `grilling-for-routine`.

```bash
dora harness new
```
30→
That grill loads `writing-for-routine` for the night prompt. Collect skills to run, skills to refer to, and the MCP URL. Then print or run one live pass.

Write the folder only after that pass, or after you accept the printed command:

```bash
dora harness new --accept --yes --slug <slug> --prompt-file <prompt.md> --mcp-url <url>
```

Most jobs need a Scalekit Agent Gateway MCP URL. Pass `--mcp-url none` when the job is a Skill script plus local creds only. After save, put secrets in `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/.env`. Dora does not copy `.env` from the original skill.
40→
The printed one-pass command looks like this:

```bash
hermes chat --toolsets mcp-scalekit --oneshot --run-budget 600 -q "…"
```

`--run-budget` is the one-pass time limit (default 10 minutes). Skills to run are passed as `--skills`. Dora refuses to overwrite an existing slug.

Dora appends a pocket-agent footer to the prompt Hermes runs. Human-visible messages end with `Sent by pocket agent <slug>`. `prompt.md` does not contain that line.
50→
A Tick has no last chat. The grill tells the night prompt to search the destination before a create, or to use a tick handoff: read `handoff.md` at the start, overwrite it at the end. Missing file means first Tick. Dora does not write that file.

## Fixed step

A Fixed step is optional. Loop-able stays first. A small loop-able job can ship with `prompt.md` only.

After one good one-pass, the grill may freeze a deterministic step into a Skill. The grill drafts. You accept. A Tick never writes files. The one-pass does not author files.

`prompt.md` names that Skill. It keeps the steps that need a new decision. It does not repeat the frozen steps.
60→
A Skill script is optional. If one exists, it lives inside that Skill. The routine has no top-level scripts directory. Do not use Hermes `--script` or `--no-agent`. Those flags cannot call Scalekit MCP tools.

## Boot the night job

```bash
dora harness boot <slug>
```

Boot tells Hermes to run this routine on a schedule. Then Dora exits. You can close that terminal.
70→
Hermes keeps a background service on this Mac. That service starts the job again when the interval is due. You do not leave a chat window open.

After boot, log in once in a real terminal. Dora does not open the browser:

```bash
hermes mcp login scalekit
```

If a later run cannot reach Scalekit, run that login again. If the Scalekit account itself is dead, open the provider link again.
80→
## Runtime watch

After `boot`, `list`, `pause`, and `resume`, Dora prints Runtime watch commands. Today those are Hermes commands. Folder-only `new` and `open` do not print them. On token or MCP fail, login is the required next command. Dora still prints the watch list.

```bash
hermes cron list
hermes cron runs
hermes logs
hermes dashboard
90→```

## Pause, resume, list, open

```bash
dora harness list
dora harness pause <slug>
dora harness resume <slug>
dora harness open <slug>
```
100→
`pause` skips later runs of that routine only. Other routines keep going. A run that already started may finish. `resume` starts later runs again. `list` shows each slug as running, paused, or none. `open` opens the routine folder.

Close the laptop and the Mac sleeps. Jobs do not run while the Mac sleeps. That is not pause. Due jobs can fire on wake if the job is not paused.

## Defaults

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| How often it runs | every 1 hour |
110→| One-pass time limit | 10 minutes |
| Night stop if the job sits idle | 10 minutes (Hermes default) |

You can change the interval and the one-pass limit per routine. A busy night job can keep going past 10 minutes if it is still working.

## Common mistakes

- Treating laptop close as `dora harness pause`. Sleep stops the clock. It does not pause the job.
- Expecting Dora to finish `hermes mcp login scalekit`. You run that in a real terminal.
- Re-running `--accept` on the same slug. Dora refuses to overwrite the folder.
120→- Expecting a Dora logs verb. Use the Runtime watch commands Dora prints.
- Using Hermes `--script` as the freeze path. A Skill script is local work inside the Skill.
- Putting a `scripts/` folder next to `prompt.md`.
- Expecting a chat app in the harness. Connectors live on a use case, not in this group.

## Related

- [Run a pocket agent](/get-started/pocket-agents/)
- [Commands](/commands/)
- [Skills](/get-started/skills/)
130→- [Hermes Agent docs](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/)

Close the laptop and the Mac sleeps. Jobs do not run while the Mac sleeps. That is not pause. Due jobs can fire on wake if the job is not paused.

## Defaults

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| How often it runs | every 1 hour |
| One-pass time limit | 10 minutes |
| Night stop if the job sits idle | 10 minutes (Hermes default) |

You can change the interval and the one-pass limit per routine. A busy night job can keep going past 10 minutes if it is still working.

## Common mistakes

- Treating laptop close as `dora harness pause`. Sleep stops the clock. It does not pause the job.
- Expecting Dora to finish `hermes mcp login scalekit`. You run that in a real terminal.
- Re-running `--accept` on the same slug. Dora refuses to overwrite the folder.
- Expecting a Dora logs verb. Use the Runtime watch commands Dora prints.
- Using Hermes `--script` as the freeze path. A Skill script is local work inside the Skill.
- Putting a `scripts/` folder next to `prompt.md`.
- Expecting a chat app in the harness. Connectors live on a use case, not in this group.

1→---
title: Run a pocket agent
description: Grill a small loop, test one pass, then boot it. The folder is a Routine.
sidebar:
  label: Pocket agents
  order: 5
---

A **pocket agent** is a small unattended loop: one job, one machine, one user. The saved folder is still a **Routine** at `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`.
10→
This page shows one use case all the way through. Install the four skills and [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/) first.

```bash
npx skills add saif-shines/doraval --yes
```

## Worked example: Slack mention, then approve the PR

You want this: poll a Slack channel. If a message mentions you, says `approve`, and has a PR link, approve that PR. Do not merge.
20→
### 1. Start

```text
/ask-dora I have a use case where I want to run a routine that looks at a slack channel and approve a pr on my behalf
```

Empty `/ask-dora` or “what can you help with” prints the map. A real idea loads `grilling-for-routine`.

### 2. Loop-able and pocket
30→
The grill asks if Slack is a poll or a webhook, and if you must confirm every PR.

You say: someone mentions you, writes `approve`, and pastes the PR link. The job approves that PR. You want a short loop later.

That is **loop-able**. Same prompt on a timer. No human on that Tick.

That is **pocket**. One job. One machine. One user.

Do not set 1 minute yet. Default is 1 hour. Change it after a good run.
40→
### 3. Lock the facts

You give:

- Channel: `#pr-review`
- Mention: `@you`
- Trigger: `@you` + `approve` + a PR link
- Action: approve only. No merge.

50→### 4. Gate

The grill still needs three answers.

1. Skills to **run**: `none` (MCP tools are enough).
2. Skills to **refer to**: `none`.
3. Scalekit Agent Gateway **MCP URL**: paste yours. Do not invent one.

```text
Skills to run: none
60→Skills to refer to: none
MCP URL: https://<your-env>.scalekit.cloud/mcp
Slug: slack-pr-approve
```

### 5. Night prompt

The grill writes `prompt.md`. It looks like this:

```text
70→1. Poll Slack channel #pr-review for new messages.
   Done-when: new items since the last tick are listed, or the list is empty.
2. Keep a message only if it mentions @you, contains the word approve, and has a pull request URL.
   Done-when: each new message is kept or skipped with a reason.
3. For each kept message, approve that pull request. Do not merge.
   Done-when: each kept PR is approved or skipped with a reason.
```

A Tick has no last chat. Prefer a search before a create. GitHub approve is already safe. A calendar create is not. Search first, or use a **tick handoff**: read `handoff.md` at the start, overwrite it at the end. Missing file means first Tick. Dora does not write that file.

80→When Hermes runs that prompt, Dora appends:

```text
Human-visible messages end with: Sent by pocket agent slack-pr-approve
```

Do not put that line in `prompt.md`. A Slack post then ends with `Sent by pocket agent slack-pr-approve`.

### 6. One pass

90→The grill prints:

```bash
dora harness new --accept --yes --slug slack-pr-approve --prompt-file <prompt.md> --mcp-url https://<your-env>.scalekit.cloud/mcp
```

Run that in a real terminal. Hermes is quiet (`-q`). The terminal can look empty. That is the first test. It is not the hourly loop.

If it sits with no output, the usual cause is a missing login. Ctrl+C, then:

100→```bash
hermes mcp login scalekit
```

Dora does not run that login. Then run the one-pass again.

Folder after accept: `~/.dora/harness/slack-pr-approve/`.

### 7. Boot and watch

110→```bash
dora harness boot slack-pr-approve
hermes mcp login scalekit
```

Dora prints Runtime watch commands:

```bash
hermes cron list
hermes cron runs
120→hermes logs
hermes dashboard
```

### 8. Check it

Post in `#pr-review`: `@you approve` and the PR link.

To avoid waiting an hour, edit `interval` in `~/.dora/harness/slack-pr-approve/routine.yml` to `1m` after a good run. Or say **run one tick** and fire one pass now.

130→Laptop close is sleep. That is not `pause`.

## Another shape: Skill script, no Gateway

Some jobs use a Skill script and an API key. They do not use Agent Gateway.

Pass `--mcp-url none`. After save, open `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/.env` in an editor and put the key there. Do not paste the key into chat.

Dora does not copy `.env` from the original skill.

140→## Common mistakes

- Treating a quiet one-pass as a hang. Wait, or Ctrl+C and run `hermes mcp login scalekit`.
- Booting before login.
- Setting a 1 minute interval during the grill.
- Expecting a Dora logs verb. Use the Runtime watch commands.
- Putting secrets in `prompt.md`.

1→# dora verbs

Same order as `dora --help`. Flags: `dora <command> --help`. Map: `dora --help --json`.
Bare noun groups **list**. Create sits on the noun (`… new`).

| Command | Job |
| --- | --- |
| `dora` | Short `--help`. First job is `dora review --quick`. |
| `dora review [path]` | Gate: structure → heuristics → Judge → sessions. Full Review adds Session health. `--quick` skips Judge and Session health. |
10→| `dora fix [path]` | Mechanical `--yes`. Judgment `--brief` / `--json` (`message`, `severity`, `hint`, optional `code` / `docUrl`). |
| `dora scan` | Workspace map. Not the empty-argv default. |
| `dora skill` | List Authored + Global Skills |
| `dora skill unused` | Unused Skills. Remove candidates are never invoked and not a Recent install. `--global` is home Skills. `--last` / `--since` override the Review window for one run. |
| `dora skill remove` / `restore` | Delete Authored or Quarantine / restore Global |
| `dora skill new` | Scaffold a Skill |
| `dora rule` | List review rules |
| `dora rule new` | Scaffold a Rule |
| `dora session` | List Sessions. `show <id>` (short id is enough if unique) |
| `dora memory` | List principles. `add` / `promote` (`promote` writes `AGENTS.md`) |
20→| `dora conflicts` | Cross-agent contradictions (`--dry-run`, then `--yes`) |
| `dora config` | List keys. `get` / `set` / `setup`. Secret `set` needs `--yes` or `--dry-run`. `identity.api_key` is minted on doraval.dev/account. Never echo it. |
| `dora agent` | List Subagents |
| `dora agent new` | Scaffold a Subagent |
| `dora plugin` | List Plugins |
| `dora plugin new` | Scaffold a Plugin |

## Naming debt (intentional)

- **`JournalConfig` / `journal:`** — historical. Prefer saying **config** in docs and new code comments. Full rename is not required for correctness.
- **`E-VAL-*` / `E-SCAN-*`** — older scan/error codes. New mechanical skill issues should stamp **rule codes** (`R0xx`) where a binding exists.
- **`agent-invoke`** — CLI agent spawn for skill exercise / prompt-gen. **Not** the judge path (judge is API or delegate only).

## Architecture vocabulary

When designing modules: **module**, **interface**, **depth**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**, **locality** (see codebase-design skill). Prefer one deep module per product concept (especially **Judge**).

## Naming debt (intentional)

- **`JournalConfig` / `journal:`** — historical. Prefer saying **config** in docs and new code comments. Full rename is not required for correctness.
- **`E-VAL-*` / `E-SCAN-*`** — older scan/error codes. New mechanical skill issues should stamp **rule codes** (`R0xx`) where a binding exists.
- **`agent-invoke`** — CLI agent spawn for skill exercise / prompt-gen. **Not** the judge path (judge is API or delegate only).

## Architecture vocabulary

When designing modules: **module**, **interface**, **depth**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**, **locality** (see codebase-design skill). Prefer one deep module per product concept (especially **Judge**).

_Avoid_: Dora on the OAuth / magic-link path; Slack, Discord, or Webflow in the harness; writing loop terms into kit CONTEXT.md.

## Naming debt (intentional)

- **`JournalConfig` / `journal:`** — historical. Prefer saying **config** in docs and new code comments. Full rename is not required for correctness.
- **`E-VAL-*` / `E-SCAN-*`** — older scan/error codes. New mechanical skill issues should stamp **rule codes** (`R0xx`) where a binding exists.
- **`agent-invoke`** — CLI agent spawn for skill exercise / prompt-gen. **Not** the judge path (judge is API or delegate only).

## Architecture vocabulary

When designing modules: **module**, **interface**, **depth**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**, **locality** (see codebase-design skill). Prefer one deep module per product concept (especially **Judge**).

name: Bun
description: Use when building, running, testing, or bundling JavaScript/TypeScript applications. Reach for Bun when you need to execute scripts, manage dependencies, run tests, or bundle code for production. Bun is a drop-in replacement for Node.js with integrated package manager, test runner, and bundler.
metadata:
    mintlify-proj: bun
    version: "1.0"
---

# Bun Skill
10→
## Product Summary

Bun is an all-in-one JavaScript/TypeScript toolkit that replaces Node.js, npm, Jest, and esbuild. It ships as a single binary with four integrated tools: a fast runtime (powered by JavaScriptCore), a package manager, a test runner, and a bundler. Key files: `bunfig.toml` (configuration), `package.json` (dependencies and scripts), `bun.lock` (lockfile). Primary CLI commands: `bun run`, `bun install`, `bun test`, `bun build`. Bun is 4x faster than Node.js at startup and 25x faster than npm at installation. See https://bun.com/docs for complete documentation.

## When to Use

- **Running scripts**: Execute `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx` files directly without compilation overhead
- **Managing dependencies**: Install, add, remove, or update npm packages with `bun install` and `bun add`
- **Running tests**: Write Jest-compatible tests with `bun test` for unit, integration, and DOM testing
20→- **Bundling code**: Bundle TypeScript, JSX, CSS, and assets for browsers or servers with `bun build`
- **Building servers**: Create HTTP servers with `Bun.serve()` with built-in routing, WebSocket support, and streaming
- **Monorepo management**: Use workspaces to manage multiple packages in a single repository
- **Replacing Node.js workflows**: Drop-in replacement for existing Node.js projects with minimal changes

## Quick Reference

### Core Commands

| Command | Purpose |
30→|---------|---------|
| `bun run <file>` | Execute a TypeScript/JavaScript file |
| `bun run <script>` | Run a package.json script |
| `bun install` | Install all dependencies from package.json |
| `bun add <pkg>` | Add a package to dependencies |
| `bun add -d <pkg>` | Add a package to devDependencies |
| `bun remove <pkg>` | Remove a package |
| `bun test` | Run all test files matching patterns |
| `bun build <entry>` | Bundle code for production |
| `bunx <pkg>` | Execute a package without installing |
40→
### File Patterns Recognized

- **Scripts**: `*.test.ts`, `*_test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `*_spec.ts`
- **Imports**: Direct imports of `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, `.html` files
- **Assets**: `.css`, `.svg`, `.png`, and other unrecognized extensions treated as files

### Configuration Files

| File | Purpose |
50→|------|---------|
| `bunfig.toml` | Bun-specific configuration (optional) |
| `package.json` | Dependencies, scripts, workspaces |
| `tsconfig.json` | TypeScript compiler options |
| `bun.lock` | Lockfile (auto-generated, commit to version control) |

### Key Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
60→| `BUN_PORT` | Default port for `Bun.serve()` |
| `PORT` | Fallback port if `BUN_PORT` not set |
| `NODE_PORT` | Another fallback port |
| `BUN_INSTALL_GLOBAL_DIR` | Directory for global package installs |

## Decision Guidance

### When to Use `bun run` vs `bun build`

| Scenario | Use |
70→|----------|-----|
| Executing a script during development | `bun run` |
| Running a package.json script | `bun run <script>` |
| Creating a production bundle for browsers | `bun build --target browser` |
| Creating a production bundle for servers | `bun build --target bun` |
| Creating a standalone executable | `bun build --compile` |

### When to Use `bun install` vs `bun add`

| Scenario | Use |
80→|----------|-----|
| Installing all dependencies from package.json | `bun install` |
| Adding a new package to the project | `bun add <pkg>` |
| Adding a dev dependency | `bun add -d <pkg>` |
| Installing globally (system-wide) | `bun add -g <pkg>` |
| Installing from git | `bun add git@github.com:user/repo.git` |

### When to Use `--watch` vs `--hot`

| Scenario | Use |
90→|----------|-----|
| Re-run a script when files change | `bun run --watch <file>` |
| Hot reload with HMR for web development | `bun --hot run <file>` |
| Re-run tests when files change | `bun test --watch` |

## Workflow

### 1. Initialize a Project
```bash
bun init my-app
100→cd my-app
```
Choose a template: Blank, React, or Library. This creates `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and a starter file.

### 2. Install Dependencies
```bash
bun install
```
Reads `package.json`, downloads packages, and creates `bun.lock`. Runs lifecycle scripts for trusted dependencies only.

110→### 3. Add New Packages
```bash
bun add react
bun add -d @types/react
```
Updates `package.json` and `bun.lock`. Use `-d` for dev dependencies, `--optional` for optional, `--peer` for peer.

### 4. Run Scripts
```bash
bun run dev
120→bun run build
bun run test
```
Executes scripts defined in `package.json`. Bun respects lifecycle hooks (`pre<script>`, `post<script>`).

### 5. Write and Run Tests
```bash
# Create a test file
echo 'import { test, expect } from "bun:test"; test("math", () => expect(2+2).toBe(4));' > math.test.ts

130→# Run tests
bun test
bun test --watch
bun test --coverage
```

### 6. Build for Production
```bash
bun build ./src/index.tsx --outdir ./dist
bun build ./src/index.tsx --outfile ./app --compile
140→```
Bundles code, handles TypeScript/JSX transpilation, tree-shakes dead code, minifies if requested.

### 7. Create an HTTP Server
```typescript
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  routes: {
    "/": () => new Response("Hello"),
    "/api/users/:id": req => new Response(`User ${req.params.id}`),
150→  },
});
console.log(`Server at ${server.url}`);
```
Run with `bun run server.ts`. Supports routing, WebSockets, streaming, and TLS.

## Common Gotchas

- **Lifecycle scripts security**: Bun does not run `postinstall` scripts by default. Add packages to `trustedDependencies` in `package.json` to allow them.
- **Node.js shebang in scripts**: Scripts with `#!/usr/bin/env node` will run with Node.js by default. Use `bun run --bun <script>` to force Bun execution.
160→- **TypeScript errors in Bun global**: Install `@types/bun` and add `"lib": ["ESNext"]` to `tsconfig.json` to fix type errors.
- **Watch mode flag placement**: Put Bun flags immediately after `bun`, not at the end: `bun --watch run dev` ✓, `bun run dev --watch` ✗
- **Lockfile format**: Bun v1.2+ uses text-based `bun.lock` by default. Older projects may have binary `bun.lockb`; migrate with `bun install --save-text-lockfile`.
- **Module resolution**: Bun supports both ESM and CommonJS. Use `"type": "module"` in `package.json` for ESM-first projects.
- **Phantom dependencies**: With `linker: "isolated"` (default for workspaces), packages can only access declared dependencies. Avoid relying on transitive dependencies.
- **Test discovery**: Tests must match patterns like `*.test.ts` or `*.spec.ts`. Files in `node_modules` are skipped automatically.
- **Bundler output**: Without `--outdir`, `bun build` returns artifacts in memory; use `--outdir` to write to disk.
- **Environment variables**: Bun auto-loads `.env` files. Disable with `env = false` in `bunfig.toml` if needed.

## Verification Checklist
170→
Before submitting work with Bun:

- [ ] Run `bun install` to verify dependencies resolve without errors
- [ ] Run `bun test` to ensure all tests pass
- [ ] Run `bun run build` (or equivalent) to verify the build succeeds
- [ ] Check `bun.lock` is committed to version control (for reproducible installs)
- [ ] Verify `bunfig.toml` settings match project requirements (if used)
- [ ] Test with `bun run <script>` to ensure scripts execute correctly
- [ ] For servers: verify `Bun.serve()` listens on the correct port and routes work
180→- [ ] For bundled code: check output files exist in `--outdir` and have expected content
- [ ] Confirm no lifecycle scripts are silently skipped (check `trustedDependencies`)
- [ ] Validate TypeScript/JSX transpilation by checking bundled output

## Resources

- **Comprehensive navigation**: https://bun.com/docs/llms.txt — Full page-by-page index of all Bun documentation
- **Runtime documentation**: https://bun.com/docs/runtime — Execute files, manage environment, use built-in APIs
- **Package manager**: https://bun.com/docs/pm/cli/install — Install, add, remove, and manage dependencies
- **Bundler**: https://bun.com/docs/bundler — Bundle TypeScript, JSX, CSS for browsers and servers
190→- **Test runner**: https://bun.com/docs/test — Write and run Jest-compatible tests with snapshots and mocking

---

> For additional documentation and navigation, see: https://bun.com/docs/llms.txt

# Bun Skill

## Product Summary

Bun is an all-in-one JavaScript/TypeScript toolkit that replaces Node.js, npm, Jest, and esbuild. - **Building servers**: Create HTTP servers with `Bun.serve()` with built-in routing, WebSocket support, and streaming

# Writing Commit Messages

## Overview

Every commit message follows a consistent format. The subject line completes the sentence: **"If applied, this commit will _\<your subject line\>_"**. When present, the body explains **why**, not what.

## Detect Project Convention First
20→
Follow existing instructions for commits if present in the repository. Check `git log --oneline -20` to see recent patterns and match the existing style.

**Project convention always wins.** The rules below are the default when no convention is detected.

- **Subject line rules, body format, URLs, issue references**: [references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md](references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md)

This skill is based on widely-accepted git commit message conventions, with inspiration from:

1→# Commit Format Reference

Complete guide to commit message formatting, line wrapping, and conventions.

## Contents
- Subject line rules
- Body format and wrapping
- Long URLs
- Issue references
10→- Conventional Commits compatibility

## Subject Line Rules

| Rule | Example | Violation | Why |
|------|---------|-----------|-----|
| Capitalize first word | `Add CPU arch filter` | `add CPU arch filter` | Sentence case always |
| Imperative mood | `Fix null pointer` | `Fixed null pointer` | Command form: Add/Fix/Remove |
| 72 char max | `Add CPU arch filter support` | `Add CPU architecture filter to scheduler...` | Hard limit |
| No trailing period | `Add user auth` | `Add user auth.` | Subject is title, not sentence |
20→| No scope prefix | `Fix null pointer in auth` | `auth: fix null pointer` | Unless Conventional Commits |
| Meaningful standalone | `Add CPU arch filter support` | `Fix #847` | Readable outside platform |

```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter scheduler support

# ❌ Wrong
added cpu arch filter scheduler support    # lowercase, past tense
```
30→
## Body Format and Wrapping

### Blank line after subject (critical)

```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter support

In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes, the scheduler
40→could not distinguish architectures.

# ❌ Wrong (no blank line)
Add CPU arch filter support
In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes...
```

### Wrap at 72 characters

Exception: URLs and code that can't be split.
50→
### Explain WHY, not WHAT

The diff shows what changed; the message explains why:

```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter support

In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes, the scheduler
60→could not distinguish architectures, causing crashes.

# ❌ Wrong (only describes WHAT)
Add CPU arch filter support

Added arch label to nodes and filter to algorithm.
```

### Describe effects and limitations

70→```bash
Add CPU arch filter support

Enables workloads to be scheduled only on compatible
architectures. Current limitation: only x86 and ARM
supported. New architectures require updating enum.
```

## Long URLs

80→Put URLs on their own line or use reference-style:

```bash
# Option 1: URL on own line
Implement the technique described at:

https://example.com/very/long/url/exceeds/72/chars

# Option 2: Reference-style
Implement the technique at [1] to prevent exhaustion.
90→
[1] https://example.com/very/long/url/exceeds/72/chars
```

## Issue References

**Only add if project uses them** (check `git log --oneline -20`).

Put in **body** on **own line** at end:

100→```bash
# ✅ Correct
Add CPU arch filter support

[explanation]

Fixes #847

# ❌ Wrong (in subject)
Fix #847: Add CPU arch filter
110→```

**Keywords:** `Fixes #N`, `Closes #N`, `Resolves #N` (GitHub/GitLab), `PROJ-123` (Jira)

## Full Example

```
Add CPU arch filter scheduler support

In a mixed environment of x86 and ARM nodes, the scheduler
120→previously could not distinguish between architectures,
leading to binary incompatibility crashes.

Add an arch label to each node and a corresponding filter
in the scheduling algorithm. This enables workloads to be
scheduled only on compatible architectures.

Current limitation: only x86 and ARM are supported. Adding
new architectures requires updating the label enum.

130→Fixes #847
```

## Conventional Commits Compatibility

If project uses Conventional Commits, use this format:

```bash
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

140→feat(scheduler): add CPU arch filter support
fix(auth): handle null session token
chore(deps): update lodash to 4.17.21
```

**Common types:**
- `feat:` - new feature
- `fix:` - bug fix
- `chore:` - maintenance
- `docs:` - documentation
150→- `refactor:` - code change (no fix/feature)
- `test:` - tests
- `perf:` - performance

All other rules still apply (imperative, 72-char limit includes prefix, body explains WHY).

## Gotchas

- **72-char limit includes type prefix** — `feat(scheduler): ` counts toward 72
- **Blank line is critical** — many tools parse on this boundary
160→- **Issue refs in body, not subject** — keeps subject meaningful
- **URLs break wrapping rule** — put on own line
- **Capitalize after colon** — `feat: Add auth` not `feat: add auth` (unless project uses lowercase)

# 55 Hermes cron tick-state (notepad, continuity, monitor, workdir, MEMORY.md)

**Question:** Hermes cron has tick-state tools (notepad, `--continuity`, `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url`, `--workdir`, MEMORY.md). Dora boots pocket agents onto Hermes. Can Dora input or leverage those capabilities in pocket-agent setup, and which ones should it?

Each Hermes cron tick is a **new agent session**. Tick-state is not conversation history. It is something Hermes **injects into this tick's prompt**, or a **file the agent can read**, or a **cheap pre-LLM hash skip**.
| Store | Who writes | Who reads next tick | What it actually is |
| Fresh session (default) | Nobody | Nothing from last tick | New `AIAgent`. No prior transcript. |
| `--workdir` | Agent via file tools in that dir | Next tick, same dir | cwd + optional `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` |

Each tick, **before** the LLM: hash exact UTF-8 bytes (no whitespace strip). Same hash → silent `no_change`, no delivery. First run or changed → inject baseline / unified diff (diff cap 4k, output cap 8k) and run the agent. Persist hash **before** the agent runs, so a failed agent does not re-alert forever. Source failure is an error, not a change.
Craft already **assumes** a last tick (`writing-for-routine` / pocket-agents example: "new items since the last tick") but never says where that watermark lives.
| Model forgets to write | Notepad and a workdir file both need the agent to persist. A forgotten write = duplicate Slack actions next tick. |

First run: missing file = empty list. Done-when: file written. No Hermes flag. No Dora code. One-pass can use the absolute path `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/last_ts` after save (folder exists only after `--accept`).

1→# Atomic Commits Reference

Each commit should do ONE logical thing. This makes code easier to review, revert, and understand.

## The Core Principle

**One commit = one logical change**

If your subject line contains "and", you probably need two commits.
10→
```bash
# ❌ Wrong — contains "and"
Refactor auth module and add user preferences endpoint

# ✅ Correct — split into two commits
Commit 1: Refactor auth module for reusability
Commit 2: Add user preferences endpoint
```

20→## Split Recommendations by Change Type

- **Refactoring** → Always separate from functional changes
- **Bug fixes** → One bug = one commit (even across multiple files)
- **Features** → One feature = one commit (or logical sub-parts)
- **Dependencies** → Group related deps, split unrelated

## Example: Good Split vs Bad Bundle

```bash
30→# ❌ Bad bundle
Refactor DB pool and add health check endpoint

Changed connection pool to singleton pattern, added
/health endpoint for load balancer checks, updated
error handling.

# ✅ Good split
Commit 1: Refactor DB connection pool to singleton

40→Previous per-request pool creation caused connection
exhaustion under high load. Switch to singleton with
configurable pool size.

Commit 2: Add health check endpoint for load balancers

Implements /health endpoint that returns 200 when DB
connection is healthy, 503 otherwise.
```

50→## Anti-Rationalizations

Don't bundle unrelated changes because:

- **"It's faster"** — Bundling saves 30 seconds now, costs hours when reverting or bisecting
- **"They're all small"** — Small unrelated changes are easier to split, not harder
- **"End of day"** — Time pressure is not a reason to violate commit hygiene

## Gotchas

60→- **Don't confuse "touches multiple files" with "multiple commits"** — a single logical change can span many files
- **When in doubt, split** — easier to squash later than to untangle a bundle
- **Use interactive rebase to split commits** — `git rebase -i` lets you edit/split

1→---
name: tdd
description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle — consult them before and during the loop, not after.

10→When exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification — "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists — and survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams — where tests go

20→A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything — agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?"

When the shape of that interface is itself in question — how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose — use the `/codebase-design` skill for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

30→- **Implementation-coupled** — mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological** — the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth — a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

- **Horizontal slicing** — writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead — one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards** — does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec** — does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?
10→

The issue tracker should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point — a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc. If they didn't specify one, ask for it.
20→
Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here — not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.) — fetch via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
30→2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.
4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".

### 3. Identify the standards sources

Anything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

On top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below — a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:

40→- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.
- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic ("possible Feature Envy"), never a hard violation — and, like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.

Each smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:

- **Mysterious Name** — a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.
- **Duplicated Code** — the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.
- **Feature Envy** — a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.
- **Data Clumps** — the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.
- **Primitive Obsession** — a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.
50→- **Repeated Switches** — the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.
- **Shotgun Surgery** — one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.
- **Divergent Change** — one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.
- **Speculative Generality** — abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.
- **Message Chains** — long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.
- **Middle Man** — a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.
- **Refused Bequest** — a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.

### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel

60→**Standards sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The full diff command and commit list.
- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full — the sub-agent has no other access to it.
- The brief: "Report — per file/hunk where relevant — (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls — documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words."

**Spec sub-agent prompt** — include:

- The diff command and commit list.
- The path or fetched contents of the spec.
70→- The brief: "Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words."

If the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.

### 5. Aggregate

Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings — the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

End with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes — that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.

80→## Why two axes

A change can pass one axis and fail the other:

- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**
- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**

Reporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.

1→# Harness management

Date: 2026-09-04
Status: ready-for-agent
Parent: [Local use-case runner](../local-use-cases/spec.md) · #79–#83 (shipped)

Grill closed 2026-09-04. Process: Matt Pocock `grilling` → `to-spec` → `to-tickets` → `implement`.

Parent issue: [#94](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/94).
10→
Tickets:

- [#95](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/95) See: job id, list, and show (frontier)
- [#96](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/96) Apply (`boot` is alias) — blocked by #95
- [#97](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/97) Logs — blocked by #95
- [#98](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/98) Remove — blocked by #95
- [#99](https://github.com/saif-shines/doraval/issues/99) Docs lockstep — blocked by #96, #97, #98

Frontier: #95. Next session: `/implement` #95. Clear context between tickets.
20→
## Problem Statement

A Routine already exists. The teammate and the coding agent cannot manage it from Dora.

`list` shows only a slug and a coarse state. There is no card for one Routine. There is no way to see that job’s ticks. Pause and resume pass a slug to a Runtime that wants a job id, so they miss the live job. A second `boot` creates a second job. There is no delete. There is no push after the folder changes.

`ask-dora` still names only `boot`, `pause`, `resume`, `list`, and `open`. An agent that must act has no copy-paste verb for apply, show, logs, or remove.

## Solution
30→
Dora stays the front desk. The folder stays the source of truth. The teammate and the agent type a **slug**. Dora maps the Runtime job id.

`apply` pushes the folder onto the Runtime job. First time it creates the job and stores the id. Later it edits that id. `boot` is the same command. Help and `ask-dora` lead with `apply`.

`list` is a table. `show` is the card for one Routine. `list <slug>` is `show`. `logs` asks with slugs, then prints that job’s ticks. `rm` stops that job, then deletes the folder.

Agents act through the same verbs. They pass a slug. They use `--yes` / `--dry-run` on writes and `--json` on reads. They do not type a hex id. They do not need a TTY picker.

## User Stories
40→
1. As a teammate, I want `dora harness list` to show slug, state, interval, and last run, so that I can scan every Routine.
2. As a teammate, I want `dora harness show <slug>` to print one card, so that I do not open the folder to learn state.
3. As a teammate, I want that card to show slug, state, interval, max tick, MCP yes or none, last run, and folder path, so that I see the contract.
4. As a teammate, I do not want the card to print the full prompt or secrets, so that `open` stays the way to read files.
5. As a teammate, I want the hex job id only in `--json`, so that the default card stays human.
6. As a teammate, I want `dora harness list <slug>` to be the same as `show`, so that a wrong guess still works.
7. As a teammate, I want bare `dora harness` to stay the list, so that the front desk does not change.
8. As a teammate, I want `dora harness apply <slug>` to push the folder onto the Runtime job, so that an edited prompt or interval actually runs.
9. As a teammate, I want a first `apply` to create the Runtime job and remember its id, so that later verbs hit the same job.
50→10. As a teammate, I want a later `apply` to edit that job, so that I do not get a second job.
11. As a teammate, I want `dora harness boot` to do the same as `apply`, so that old commands and old skill lines still work.
12. As a teammate, I want help and `ask-dora` to lead with `apply`, so that new readers learn one word.
13. As a teammate, I do not want `dora harness set`, so that there is one way to change the folder: edit the files.
14. As a teammate, I want to change `prompt.md` or `routine.yml` with `open` or an editor, then `apply`, so that the folder stays the editor.
15. As a coding agent, I want to write those files and then run `dora harness apply <slug> --yes`, so that I can finish without a TTY.
16. As a teammate, I want `apply` to start the Runtime gateway if it is down, so that a first attach still works.
17. As a teammate, I want missing Hermes on `apply` to print official install steps and stop, so that Dora does not fake a push.
18. As a teammate, I want a dead stored id to make `apply` create a new job and write the new id, so that I can attach again.
19. As a teammate, I want `pause`, `resume`, and `logs` to say the job is gone when the id is dead, so that I know to `apply`.
60→20. As a teammate, I want `rm` to delete the folder even when the job is already gone, so that a leftover folder is not stuck.
21. As a teammate, I want `rm` to stop if the job is still there and remove fails, so that I do not orphan a running job.
22. As a teammate with old Routines that have no stored id, I want the first verb that needs the id to match Runtime name to slug and write the id, so that I do not get a second job.
23. As a teammate, I want pause and resume to use that stored id, so that they hit the live job.
24. As a teammate, I want `dora harness logs` to list slugs and let me pick, so that I never type a hex id.
25. As a teammate, I want that pick to run the Runtime’s per-job run history for that id, so that I see ticks for that Routine only.
26. As a teammate, I do not want `logs` to dump the global Runtime agent log, so that I am not reading every job at once.
27. As a teammate, I want `dora harness logs <slug>` to skip the picker, so that I can type the slug I already know.
28. As a teammate, I want `dora harness rm <slug>` to stop that job and then delete the folder, so that delete is one verb.
29. As a teammate, I want `rm` to require `--yes` (or a TTY confirm), so that a slip does not wipe a Routine.
70→30. As a teammate, I want bare `pause`, `resume`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` to pick from slugs when I am on a TTY, so that I do not remember names.
31. As a teammate, I want `rm` after a pick to still need `--yes`, so that a pick is not a delete.
32. As a coding agent, I want no picker when there is no TTY, so that I do not hang.
33. As a coding agent, I want that no-TTY path to print slugs, exit `2`, and print the next command with a slug, so that I can retry.
34. As a coding agent, I want every new or changed verb in `dora --help --json` with a copy-paste example, so that I have a live map.
35. As a coding agent, I want writes (`apply`, `boot`, `rm`) to refuse me unless I pass `--yes` or `--dry-run`, so that I do not write by accident.
36. As a coding agent, I want reads (`list`, `show`, `logs`, `pause`, `resume`) to accept `--json`, so that I get one object or one list on stdout.
37. As a coding agent, I want to type only a slug, so that I never handle a Runtime job id.
38. As a coding agent, I want a next command printed after each verb, so that I know the next act.
39. As a coding agent, I want exit `0` on success, `1` on a failed act, and `2` when I could not run (no slug, no Hermes when required, omitted `--yes` on a write), so that I can branch.
80→40. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want that skill to name `apply`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` for an existing Routine, so that I do not load the grill.
41. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want `boot` still accepted as the apply alias, so that old prompts work.
42. As a teammate, I want `review-with-dora` and `grilling-for-routine` to name the same verbs, so that the four shipped skills do not lie.
43. As a first reader, I want website `/commands/harness`, Connect/pocket-agent pages if they name verbs, and the README catalog to match the binary, so that docs lockstep holds.
44. As a teammate, I want interval on apply to become the Runtime schedule, so that a yaml change is real.
45. As a teammate, I want max tick to stay as it is today (one-pass budget / Runtime idle), so that we do not invent a new timeout flag.
46. As a teammate, I want `open` unchanged, so that I can still edit files by hand.
47. As a teammate, I want `new` unchanged, so that create stays the grill path.
48. As a teammate, I want laptop close to stay sleep, not pause, so that v1 meaning does not change.
49. As a teammate, I want Dora to stay off the OAuth / magic-link path, so that I still run Runtime login in a real terminal.
90→50. As a doraval maintainer, I want this spec in its own file, so that the shipped v1 spec stays history.
51. As a doraval maintainer, I want rename parked, so that this pass stays small.
52. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `apply` to print the Runtime commands and write nothing, so that I can preview.
53. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `rm` to print the plan and delete nothing, so that I can preview.
54. As a teammate, I want list state `none` when there is no Runtime job, so that an unbooted folder is visible.
55. As a teammate, I want list state running or paused from the Runtime when the id is known, so that the table matches the timer.
56. As a teammate, I want last run taken from the Runtime list when present, so that Dora does not invent a second history store.

41. As a coding agent using `ask-dora`, I want `boot` still accepted as the apply alias, so that old prompts work.
42. As a teammate, I want `review-with-dora` and `grilling-for-routine` to name the same verbs, so that the four shipped skills do not lie.
43. As a first reader, I want website `/commands/harness`, Connect/pocket-agent pages if they name verbs, and the README catalog to match the binary, so that docs lockstep holds.
44. As a teammate, I want interval on apply to become the Runtime schedule, so that a yaml change is real.
45. As a teammate, I want max tick to stay as it is today (one-pass budget / Runtime idle), so that we do not invent a new timeout flag.
46. As a teammate, I want `open` unchanged, so that I can still edit files by hand.
47. As a teammate, I want `new` unchanged, so that create stays the grill path.
48. As a teammate, I want laptop close to stay sleep, not pause, so that v1 meaning does not change.
49. As a teammate, I want Dora to stay off the OAuth / magic-link path, so that I still run Runtime login in a real terminal.
50. As a doraval maintainer, I want this spec in its own file, so that the shipped v1 spec stays history.
51. As a doraval maintainer, I want rename parked, so that this pass stays small.
52. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `apply` to print the Runtime commands and write nothing, so that I can preview.
53. As a coding agent, I want `--dry-run` on `rm` to print the plan and delete nothing, so that I can preview.
54. As a teammate, I want list state `none` when there is no Runtime job, so that an unbooted folder is visible.
55. As a teammate, I want list state running or paused from the Runtime when the id is known, so that the table matches the timer.
56. As a teammate, I want last run taken from the Runtime list when present, so that Dora does not invent a second history store.

## Implementation Decisions

- This is an addendum pass on the shipped harness. Hermes stays the only Runtime. Dora does not own a timer.
- The teammate-facing key is the slug. The Runtime-facing key is the job id (12-char hex on each create). Dora stores that id on the Routine after a successful create or a successful name backfill.
- Folder wins when the folder and the job disagree. `apply` is the push. There is no pull from the Runtime into the folder.
- `apply` and `boot` are one implementation. Canonical name in help, `dora --help --json`, and `ask-dora` is `apply`. `boot` remains a working alias.
- First `apply` (no stored id, and no name match): ensure the Runtime gateway is up, create one job from the folder (name = slug, schedule from interval, prompt from the folder, skills to run attached), parse the new id, store it, exit.
- Later `apply` (stored id still on the Runtime): edit that job’s schedule, prompt, and skills from the folder. Do not create.
- Stored id missing on the Runtime: create, store the new id (same as first apply).
- No stored id, but a Runtime job name equals the slug: write that id, then edit. Do not create a second job.
- Pause and resume use the stored id. They do not pass the slug to the Runtime.
- `logs` with a slug (or after a pick) runs the Runtime per-job run history for that id. It does not wrap the global agent log.
- `rm` removes that id on the Runtime if the job exists, then deletes the Routine folder. If remove fails and the job still exists, stop and keep the folder. If the job is already gone, delete the folder.
- `rm` and `apply` are writes. Detected agents need `--yes` or `--dry-run`.
- Bare verbs on a TTY pick from slugs. `rm` after a pick still needs `--yes`. No TTY: no picker; print slugs; exit `2`; print the next command with a slug.
- `list` columns: slug, state, interval, last run. State is running, paused, or none.
- `show` card: slug, state, interval, max tick, MCP yes or none, last run, folder path. Hex id only in `--json`. No full prompt. No secrets. No `.env`.
- `list <slug>` is `show`.
- No `set`. No `rename` in this pass.
- Interval maps to the Runtime schedule flag. Max tick is unchanged from v1 (one-pass budget / Runtime idle env).
- Agent contract is required: every new or changed verb on `dora --help --json` with an example; slug only; `--json` on reads; `--yes` / `--dry-run` on writes; next command after each verb; exits `0` / `1` / `2` as in the stories.
- Docs lockstep in the same change as the verbs: README command catalog, website harness command page, `ask-dora`, `review-with-dora`, `grilling-for-routine` (and `writing-for-routine` only if it names harness verbs).
- Do not bump the version unless the user asks for a release.

## Testing Decisions

A good test checks what a teammate or an agent can see, or what Dora writes to the Routine folder. It does not start a live Runtime gateway in CI. It does not run a real OAuth dance.

### Seams

1. **Primary seam: `dora harness` CLI.** Assert help text, `dora --help --json` examples, missing-Hermes install steps, `--yes` / `--dry-run` write gate, `--json` shapes, exit codes, picker vs no-TTY, and the Runtime argument lists Dora would run for apply (create vs edit), pause, resume, logs, and rm. Prefer the existing harness CLI tests and a fake Runtime binary on `PATH`.
2. **Shared artifact: Routine folder.** Assert the stored job id is written on create and on name backfill. Assert `rm` deletes the folder only when the spec allows. Do not assert Runtime job JSON schema beyond what Dora is specified to write.
3. **Shipped skills.** Assert `ask-dora` and the review/grill skills name `apply`, `show`, `logs`, and `rm` for an existing Routine, and still accept `boot`. Assert `dora review --quick` on those skill directories still exits 0.

Do not add a new seam. Do not parse live Hermes in CI.

### Modules under test

- Harness group (CLI behavior).
- Routine folder read/write (id field, rm).
- Runtime command builder (create vs edit vs pause vs resume vs remove vs runs).
- Shipped skills (named verbs).

### Prior art

- Existing harness CLI tests with a fake `hermes` on `PATH`.
- `dora --help --json` / capabilities tests for new examples.
- Docs lockstep tests that already pin harness wording.

## Out of Scope

- Rename of a slug or a Runtime job name.
- `dora harness set` or any second edit API.
- A Dora verb that wraps the global Runtime agent log.
- A repo of Routines, a git remote on the folder, a copy into skillkit.
- Config UI, Config sync, identity probe.
- A second Runtime (Claude, Grok, OpenCode).
- Dora installing Hermes.
- Dora sitting on the OAuth / magic-link path.
- Changing max tick mapping to a new Runtime flag.
- Rewriting the v1 spec.
- A version bump unless the user asks.

## Further Notes

Parent v1: `.scratch/local-use-cases/spec.md`.

Live Runtime (fact, 2026-09-04): `cron edit` and `cron remove` exist. `pause`, `resume`, `edit`, `remove`, and `runs` take a job id. `cron list` prints the hex id and `[active]` on one line and `Name:` on the next. Last run is on that list. v1 list parse and v1 pause-by-slug do not match that output. This pass must.

Research already in tree: agent-browser CLI notes (`docs/research-notes/46-agent-browser-cli-ux.md`, `50-cli-command-structure.md`); Hermes tick-state (`docs/research-notes/55-hermes-tick-state.md`).

Next: `/implement` #95 in a fresh session. Then #96, #97, and #98. Then #99.

_Avoid_: calling a login a Session; treating “dora is installed” as Connected; a local UI as the destination.

## Harness (shipped)

220→`dora harness` is the front desk. The Runtime runs the Loop. Today the Runtime is Hermes. 2026-08-31.

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Routine** | Saved folder at `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/`. The only product object. _Avoid_: pack. |
| **Loop** | The same unattended prompt on an interval. The Runtime's timer. Default 1 hour. |
| **Run** | One unattended pass of a Loop. The Runtime starts it on the interval. Not the one-pass test. _Avoid_: tick; night tick as a second object. |
| **Runtime** | The background agent that runs a Loop. Today that agent is Hermes. Dora prints that Runtime's watch commands. _Avoid_: calling Hermes the product; a second Runtime in this pass. |
| **Max run** | One-pass wall clock via the Runtime. Default 10 minutes. Night idle cap is the Runtime's idle timeout (Hermes: `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`, default 600s). Flag is still `--max-tick`. |
| **Harness** | Verbs: `new`, `apply`, `pause`, `resume`, `list`, `show`, `logs`, `open`, `rm`. `boot` is an alias of `apply`. |
230→| **Apply** | Push the Routine folder onto the Runtime job. Create or edit. _Avoid_: set; sync; upsert as a user word. |
| **Show** | The card for one Routine. `list <slug>` is the same command. _Avoid_: inspect; status as a second verb. |
| **Remove** | Stop the Runtime job, then delete the Routine folder. Verb: `rm`. |
| **Skill script** | A helper file inside a Skill folder. The Skill names the path. The routine has no top-level scripts directory. _Avoid_: routine script; Hermes `--script`. |
| **Fixed step** | A deterministic routine step stored in a Skill. `prompt.md` names that Skill. It does not repeat the step. _Avoid_: programmatize as a noun; Judgment (that word is a Dora Finding). |
| **Pocket** | Size check on a Routine idea. One job, one machine, one user. The night prompt must be specific. |
| **Pocket agent** | Reader name for that small loop. The saved folder is still a Routine. _Avoid_: a second folder type. |
| **Run handoff** | File `handoff.md` in the routine folder. Next Run reads it. This Run overwrites it. Missing file means first Run. Prefer the destination as the store. _Avoid_: Hermes notepad-with-slug; MEMORY.md as a cursor. |

_Avoid_: Dora on the OAuth / magic-link path; Slack, Discord, or Webflow in the harness; writing loop terms into kit CONTEXT.md.
240→
## Naming debt (intentional)

- **`JournalConfig` / `journal:`** — historical. Prefer saying **config** in docs and new code comments. Full rename is not required for correctness.
- **`E-VAL-*` / `E-SCAN-*`** — older scan/error codes. New mechanical skill issues should stamp **rule codes** (`R0xx`) where a binding exists.
- **`agent-invoke`** — CLI agent spawn for skill exercise / prompt-gen. **Not** the judge path (judge is API or delegate only).
- **`--max-tick` / `max_tick` / `maxTick`** — product word is **Run**. Flag and YAML stay.

## Architecture vocabulary

250→When designing modules: **module**, **interface**, **depth**, **seam**, **adapter**, **leverage**, **locality** (see codebase-design skill). Prefer one deep module per product concept (especially **Judge**).

1→# 55 Hermes cron tick-state (notepad, continuity, monitor, workdir, MEMORY.md)

_Research · 2026-09-02 · Local Hermes source + `--help` + official docs. Research only. Does not change product code._

**Question:** Hermes cron has tick-state tools (notepad, `--continuity`, `--monitor-script` / `--monitor-url`, `--workdir`, MEMORY.md). Dora boots pocket agents onto Hermes. Can Dora input or leverage those capabilities in pocket-agent setup, and which ones should it?

**Pinned binary:** local Hermes Agent **v0.20.6** (2026.8.27), upstream `32fe1293`, local `44656326` (+1 carried commit), install `/Users/saif/.hermes/hermes-agent`, PATH `/Users/saif/.local/bin/hermes`. **732 commits behind** at capture. Official pages: [cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/cron), [cron internals](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/cron-internals), [automate-with-cron](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/guides/automate-with-cron), [memory](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/memory).

Dora code under review: `src/core/hermes.ts` (includes `8076419` footer), `src/cli/commands/harness.ts`, `src/core/routine.ts`, `skills/writing-for-routine/SKILL.md`, `skills/grilling-for-routine/SKILL.md`, `apps/website/content/get-started/pocket-agents.mdx`. Prior note: [`54-hermes-provider.md`](./54-hermes-provider.md).
10→
**Trust rule:** Dora must speak the installed binary. When live docs and local `--help` / source disagree, this note trusts the local tree.

---

## Mental model

Each Hermes cron tick is a **new agent session**. Tick-state is not conversation history. It is something Hermes **injects into this tick's prompt**, or a **file the agent can read**, or a **cheap pre-LLM hash skip**.

| Store | Who writes | Who reads next tick | What it actually is |
20→|-------|------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Fresh session (default) | Nobody | Nothing from last tick | New `AIAgent`. No prior transcript. |
| Notepad | Agent via `hermes cron notepad <job_id> set` (terminal CLI; no model tool) | Scheduler prepends KV if non-empty | Per-**hex job id** SQLite, 16 KB/key, 64 KB/job |
| `--continuity` | Hermes, after a run that produced output | Scheduler prepends last `*.md` output (8k cap) | Last **report text**, not a cursor |
| Monitor hash | Scheduler, from script/URL bytes | Unchanged → **no LLM**. Changed → diff block | Exact-byte SHA-256 skip |
| `--workdir` | Agent via file tools in that dir | Next tick, same dir | cwd + optional `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` |
| MEMORY.md / USER.md | Agent `memory` tool | Every session, including cron | Shared profile notes. Not per-job. Not a cursor. |

Dora already owns a folder: `~/.dora/harness/<slug>/` (`prompt.md`, `routine.yml`, copied skills, optional `.env`). Hermes job **name** is that slug. Hermes job **id** is a new 12-char hex on every `cron create`.

30→---

## 1. Default isolation: fresh session

Default cron is amnesia for the **conversation**. Official cron page: jobs "run in fresh agent sessions with the normal static tool list." Official internals: "Create fresh `AIAgent` session (no conversation history)." Local internals: no previous-run transcript; prompt must be self-contained; `cronjob` toolset disabled.

Local fire path still **does** load profile memory (`skip_memory=False`) and `SOUL.md`. It does **not** load project context files unless `--workdir` is set (`skip_context_files=not bool(_job_workdir)`).

So: not a blank model. It is a blank **thread**. Preferences in MEMORY.md can leak in. Last Slack ts cannot, unless one of the stores above is used.

40→Cron also disables `messaging` and `clarify` always, and `cronjob` unless `cron.allow_agent_scheduling` is on. Terminal stays available. That is how notepad writes are supposed to happen.

---

## 2. Hermes mechanisms for "already seen this Slack message"

### Notepad (durable KV)

**How write.** No model tool. The running agent shells `hermes cron notepad <job_id> set <key> <value>`. Local CLI takes `job_id` as a **raw string**. It does **not** call `resolve_job_ref`. A slug write and a hex-id write are different rows.

50→**How inject.** `render_notepad_section(job["id"])` — the **hex id**, never the name. Empty or missing DB → `""` so unused jobs stay cache-identical. Non-empty prepends:

```
## Job notepad (persistent across runs)
… `hermes cron notepad {hex_id} set <key> <value>` …
- last_ts: …
```

**Caps.** Key ≤ 128 chars. Value ≤ 16 KB UTF-8. Job total (keys+values) ≤ 64 KB. Oversize raises `ValueError` and leaves the store untouched.

60→**job_id.** Store PK is `(job_id, key)`. `remove_job` clears rows for the **canonical hex id** only. Official published cron pages (live fetch + local `website/docs`) do **not** document notepad. Trust `hermes cron notepad --help` and `cron/notepad.py`.

**First run.** Empty → no notepad block → the agent is not taught the CLI or the hex id unless Dora (or the night prompt) says so.

**Oneshot.** Inject lives only in the cron scheduler prompt assembly. `hermes chat --oneshot` does not prepend notepad.

### `--continuity` (last output)

CLI flag. Stored as reserved `context_from` entry `"self"`. At fire time `"self"` becomes this job's hex id. Hermes reads the newest `~/.hermes/cron/output/{id}/*.md`, truncates at **8000 characters**, prepends "Your previous run's output" / "avoid repeating what was already reported."

70→**First run:** no output dir → silent skip. Prompt unchanged.

This is the last **delivered report**, not a Slack watermark. A long Slack dump can truncate the cursor away. Official cron page matches local `--help` here.

### Monitor hash skip

`--monitor-script` (path under `~/.hermes/scripts/`) or `--monitor-url` (bounded GET, 30s, 256 KiB). Mutually exclusive. Incompatible with `--no-agent`.

Each tick, **before** the LLM: hash exact UTF-8 bytes (no whitespace strip). Same hash → silent `no_change`, no delivery. First run or changed → inject baseline / unified diff (diff cap 4k, output cap 8k) and run the agent. Persist hash **before** the agent runs, so a failed agent does not re-alert forever. Source failure is an error, not a change.

80→Wrong tool for "new Slack messages since ts." Slack MCP is not a stable byte source. Scripts must live in Hermes' scripts dir, not the routine folder. Grill already forbids Hermes `--script` / `--no-agent`.

### `--workdir`

Absolute existing directory at create/update. `~` expands. Relative paths rejected. Sets `TERMINAL_CWD` so terminal / file / code_exec use that dir. Injects `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` from it. Does **not** auto-load that folder's `.env` (Hermes reloads `~/.hermes/.env` via `load_hermes_dotenv`).

Local 0.20.6: workdir jobs go on the **sequential** pool and take a process-global cwd lock. Live official cron page says workdir jobs stay on the parallel pool. **Trust local source.** Many Dora jobs with workdir will queue behind each other.

If the dir vanishes later, the scheduler logs a warning and runs without it.

90→`hermes chat --help` has **no** `--workdir`. One-pass cannot share this flag.

### MEMORY.md

`~/.hermes/memories/MEMORY.md` (2,200 chars) + `USER.md` (1,375). Loaded every session, including cron. Official automate-with-cron: "Persistent memory does load… but don't rely on it for job-critical details." Official memory page: do not save session ephemera. Shared across **all** jobs on the profile. A Slack ts here is the wrong store.

---

## 3. What Dora enables today (exact argv)

100→From `bootArgs` / `onePassArgs` / `hermesPrompt` and `src/core/hermes.test.ts` (current main, including `8076419`):

**One-pass** (`dora harness new --run-one-pass`):

```
hermes chat [--toolsets mcp-scalekit] --oneshot --run-budget <sec> [--skills <dir> …] -q "<prompt>\n\nHuman-visible messages end with: Sent by pocket agent <slug>"
```

**Boot** (`dora harness boot <slug>`):

110→```
hermes gateway install
hermes gateway start
# if MCP:
hermes mcp add scalekit --url <url> --auth oauth
hermes mcp test scalekit
hermes tools enable mcp-scalekit --platform cron

# Writing Commit Messages

## Overview

Every commit message follows a consistent format. The subject line completes the sentence: **"If applied, this commit will _\<your subject line\>_"**. When present, the body explains **why**, not what.

## Detect Project Convention First
20→
Follow existing instructions for commits if present in the repository. Check `git log --oneline -20` to see recent patterns and match the existing style.

**Project convention always wins.** The rules below are the default when no convention is detected.

## References

Consider the following references when creating new commit messages:
- **Subject line rules, body format, URLs, issue references**: [references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md](references/COMMIT_FORMAT.md)
